question: Which host filesystem policy contract should OpenClaw standardize for this issue, and should the first version cover arbitrary shell/exec access or explicitly split that into a separate contract?
rationale: Current main has only `tools.fs.workspaceOnly`, while open implementation candidates propose different public config shapes and leave different security boundaries around exec; automation cannot safely choose that product and security contract.

options.title: Standardize a `tools.fs` PathGuard contract and split exec
options.body: Define the file/media/apply_patch boundary under `tools.fs` with canonical deny-wins path semantics, document exec as out of scope for v1, and keep the exec-specific work on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/74379.

options.title: Adopt a typed roots model instead
options.body: Use a `tools.fs.roots` style contract if maintainers prefer explicit `file`/`dir` and `ro`/`rw` roots over broad allow/deny path globs.

options.title: Defer to OS or sandbox backends
options.body: Keep the current `workspaceOnly` model and recommend Docker, SSH, or local-user isolation for stronger host boundaries, accepting that native host allow/deny remains unavailable.

recommendation.title: Standardize a `tools.fs` PathGuard contract and split exec
recommendation.body: Define the file/media/apply_patch boundary under `tools.fs` with canonical deny-wins path semantics, document exec as out of scope for v1, and keep the exec-specific work on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/74379.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent source, history, and discussion signal around the current filesystem policy contract.
